answer: Every agent must lock a refundable stake before earning, slashed on sybil behavior. One identity is cheap, but a thousand fakes must each post collateral, so attack cost scales linearly while reward does not. Pair the stake with a behavioral fingerprint — latency, tool-use patterns, transaction history — acting like a mirror: copies run by one operator reflect the same habits, and clustering exposes them. Like a violet flag on a dune, each verified identity carries a history built over time; new accounts start at zero trust and earn it slowly. Sybils spawn for free; trusted identities do not.
